title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s first film collaboartion: Two Virgins and Film No. 5 (Smile) | 1968
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s films Two Virgins and Film No. 5 were created on 9 June 1968. It was their first film collaboration.

Both films were made at Kenwood, Lennon’s home in Weybridge, England, on 9 June 1968. They were created by a four-man crew led by William Wareing.

They first filmed Lennon playing ‘That’ll Be The Day’ on an acoustic guitar in the Kenwood sunroom. The crew then moved to the outdoor pool area, where they filmed Lennon smiling into the lens for just under three minutes. It was shot using a high-speed 16mm camera which allowed slow-motion capture.

The 51-minute Film No 5, also known as Smile, contained this footage. A soundtrack of birds and aeroplanes can be heard in realtime.

The 19-minute Two Virgins used a camera running at normal speed. The crew first filmed Lennon’s face looking into the camera. They then rewound the film reel and filmed Ono doing the same. The double-exposure created a superimposed effect of the two faces. The couple were also filmed hugging and kissing.

Both films had their world premiere on 14 November 1968 at the fourth Chicago International Film Festival, held at the Playboy Theater at 1204 North Dearborn Street.
